# Generated by iptables-save v1.8.10 on Thu Aug 28 20:00:00 2026
# A firewall someone "opened to test" and never closed: an unconditional
# -A INPUT -j ACCEPT sits above the real rules. It opens the box (permissive
# -accept flags it) AND every rule below it is dead code — the rate-limited
# ssh accept, the INVALID drop and the prefixed LOG all never run. The admin
# reads the ruleset and believes ssh is throttled and drops are logged.
*filter
:INPUT DROP [0:0]
:FORWARD DROP [0:0]
:OUTPUT ACCEPT [0:0]
-A INPUT -i lo -j ACCEPT
-A INPUT -m conntrack --ctstate ESTABLISHED,RELATED -j ACCEPT
-A INPUT -j ACCEPT
-A INPUT -p tcp --dport 22 -m conntrack --ctstate NEW -m recent --set --name SSH
-A INPUT -p tcp --dport 22 -m conntrack --ctstate NEW -m recent --update --seconds 60 --hitcount 4 --name SSH -j DROP
-A INPUT -p tcp --dport 22 -j ACCEPT
-A INPUT -m conntrack --ctstate INVALID -j DROP
-A INPUT -m limit --limit 5/min -j LOG --log-prefix "input-drop: "
COMMIT
